11/G.goal: Explain how cybersickness in virtual environments arises and how its occurrence and severity can be measured and evaluated.
11/G.achieves: It gives the learner foundational knowledge for identifying discomfort risks and selecting appropriate assessment methods when designing, implementing, or optimizing an XR system.

11/O1.goal: Explain how visual motion, locomotion methods, control, display and content characteristics, and exposure factors influence the onset and severity of cybersickness in virtual environments.
11/O1.achieves: It helps the learner understand a key psycho-physiological issue and anticipate which VR design or content choices may increase user discomfort.

11/O2.goal: Describe the input-process-output framework for measuring cybersickness, its four input categories, and the distinction between manual and machine-learning-based evaluation.
11/O2.achieves: It enables the learner to choose and interpret sickness questionnaires, physiological signals, behavioral measures, and model-based assessments when evaluating an XR experience.
